title: Finite reduction preserves normalized DNC comparison
statement:
Fix the finite-coefficient purity conventions [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $B=A_{E,m}$ with $1\le m\le n$. Work on the small pro-etale sites in the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories and put $Q_T=(-)\otimes_A^LB$. Let $S,V$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, $g:V\to S$ smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$, and $s:S\hookrightarrow V$ a closed section, $gs=\operatorname{id}_S$. Let $\pi_N:N_s\to S$ be its normal bundle with zero section $0_N$ [def-pur-normal-bundle]. For $R=A,B$, use the section invariants [def-pur-section-invariant]
$$C_R(g,s)=Ls^*Rg_R^!R_S,\qquad C_R(\pi_N,0_N)=L0_N^*R\pi_{N,R}^!R_S.$$
Let $\delta_R:C_R(g,s)\xrightarrow\sim C_R(\pi_N,0_N)$ be the unique DNC comparison of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance], normalized as the identity on the standard section invariant in etale coordinates carrying the pair near its section to $(\mathbf A^d_S\to S,0)$. Let $q_{g,s}:Q_SC_A(g,s)\xrightarrow\sim C_B(g,s)$ and $q_N:Q_SC_A(\pi_N,0_N)\xrightarrow\sim C_B(\pi_N,0_N)$ be the composites of the pullback and exceptional coefficient comparisons [lem-fix-operation-reduction, lem-coef-finite-exceptional]. Then
$$q_N\circ Q_S(\delta_A)=\delta_B\circ q_{g,s}.$$
Moreover, etale-locally on $S$, for etale coordinates carrying the pair near its section to the standard pair $(p_d:\mathbf A^d_S\to S,0)$ as in [thm-pur-dnc-invariance], the etale-localization identifications of $C_R(g,s)$ and of $C_R(\pi_N,0_N)$ with $C_R(p_d,0)$, for $R=A,B$, carry both $q_{g,s}$ and $q_N$ to the composite comparison $q_{p_d,0}:Q_SC_A(p_d,0)\xrightarrow\sim C_B(p_d,0)$ of the standard pair, formed in the same way.

source.place: Proof Step 3: finite reduction of normalized DNC gluing; normalization characterized in sk-thm-dnc/thm-pur-dnc-invariance.proof.md; agent-written extraction of returned Step 4

proof.text: Choose a common initial coefficient ring $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$. Indeed [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] gives $|\ell|_E=|\ell|_\ell=\ell^{-1}<1$ and $\mathfrak m_E=(\varpi_E)$, so $\ell=\varpi_E a$ for some $a\in\mathcal O_E$. Thus $\ell^n=\varpi_E^na^n$ annihilates $A$ and also its quotient $B$. These rings are finite by [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients]; its hypotheses for $\mathcal O_E$ follow from the DVR and finite residue field assertions of [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. Consequently the canonical unital maps factor as $R\to A\to B$. For $D=A,B$ write $T_D=(-)\otimes_R^LD$, and retain $Q=(-)\otimes_A^LB$. By [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](1),(2),(4), these are functors on the stated bounded constructible finite-Tor domains, preserve isomorphisms, and have natural associators $QT_A\simeq T_B$. No flatness of any coefficient map is asserted.

source.place: Proof (1): use a common finite initial ring; explicit annihilator calculation

proof.text: For either pair $H=(g,s)$ or $H=(\pi_N,0_N)$ write $t_D^H:T_DC_R(H)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_D(H)$ for the comparison in [lem-pur-dnc-coefficient-transport], applied separately to $R\to A$ and $R\to B$. Its normal-bundle clause supplies the second pair as well as the first; the smooth closed-section hypotheses, separated finite-type schemes and finite rings are exactly those of this item and Step 1. We identify the exceptional comparison for $A\to B$ in that notation with the one in our statement. First, $Rg^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] (statement) and $g_D^!$ of [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation] (tool) are right adjoints of the same $R\bar g_*j_!$ on the same $\Dctf$ objects, so Yoneda identifies them uniquely compatibly with counits; the two $C_D$ and all transposes below are identified along it. By [lem-coef-finite-exceptional], its counit equation, after composing with the inverse compact-support coefficient comparison, says that it is the adjunction transpose of $Q\epsilon_A$ followed by that inverse. This is precisely the defining transpose in [det-sp-reduction-exceptional]. Both use the canonical compact-support tensor comparison: [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] specifies that map for the quotient rings, and [det-sp-reduction-direct-image] specifies the same proper-counit mate followed by the open-extension tensor comparison at a compactification. Fix the same compactification in these descriptions. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection identifies the exceptional maps. Their pullbacks along the section, with the canonical pullback/tensor comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction], therefore give exactly $q_H$ of the item.

source.place: Step 2: identify the specified coefficient maps by their counit transposes

proof.text:
Apply only clause (2), the coefficient-composition assertion, of [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities] to $R\to A\to B$, first for $g$ and then for $\pi_N$, at the coefficient unit. Their smoothness, relative dimension and separated finite-type hypotheses hold; the normal-bundle application is also one of the smooth maps in [lem-pur-dnc-coefficient-transport]. Pull this composition identity back along the respective section. For the coefficient maps $R\to A$ and $R\to B$, which are not finite reductions $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$, the pullback/tensor comparison is the canonical one of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] (the one used to define $t_D^H$ in the tool); on flat K-flat representatives it is the balancing isomorphism $s^{-1}P\otimes_RD\cong s^{-1}(P\otimes_RD)$, so it commutes with the scalar associators termwise. For $A\to B$, compatibility of pullback and tensor, including tensor associativity, is [lem-fix-operation-reduction]; the natural scalar associator is [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](4). Under these identifications the identity becomes, for each $H$,
$$t_B^H=q_H\circ Q(t_A^H).$$
This is an equality of the specified maps, not a choice of an isomorphism between their sources and targets. All subsequent equations suppress these same natural associators. The purity clause (3) of the coefficient-composition node is not used.

Apply the final DNC identity of [lem-pur-dnc-coefficient-transport] to each of $R\to D$, $D=A,B$:
$$\delta_D\circ t_D^{g,s}=t_D^N\circ T_D(\delta_R).$$
Here $R$ is the purity coefficient ring at $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, level $n$. The node's directly constructed comparison over $D$ is identity-normalized in the same etale coordinate charts, by its constant-family chart clause. It is therefore the $\delta_D$ of this item by the uniqueness assertion of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance], applied at the eligible coefficient rings $A_{E,n}$ and $A_{E,m}$. This identifies actual normalized maps; no assertion that arbitrary isomorphisms between the section invariants agree is needed.

source.place: Proof (2): coefficient-independent DNC normalization; thm-pur-dnc-invariance.proof.md uniqueness

proof.text:
Put $G=(g,s)$ and $N=(\pi_N,0_N)$. The two identities of Step 4 and the cocycle of Step 3 give
$$\begin{aligned}
\delta_Bq_GQ(t_A^G)&=\delta_Bt_B^G
=t_B^NT_B(\delta_R)\\
&=q_NQ(t_A^N)T_B(\delta_R)
=q_NQ\bigl(t_A^NT_A(\delta_R)\bigr)\\
&=q_NQ(\delta_At_A^G)
=q_NQ(\delta_A)Q(t_A^G).
\end{aligned}$$
Naturality of the scalar associator in [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](4) justifies the middle equality. Its functoriality clause justifies applying $Q$ to the equality in Step 4. The map $Q(t_A^G)$ is invertible, so cancel it on the right. This proves exactly $q_NQ(\delta_A)=\delta_Bq_G$.

source.place: Step 3: deduce the quotient DNC square by coefficient composition and cancellation

proof.text:
For the additional local assertion fix any of the etale coordinate localizations of the pair in the statement, with base $S'$. Let $P=(p_d,0)$ over $S'$ and let $\lambda_D^H$ denote its specified identification from the localized invariant of $H$ to $C_D(P)$, for $H=G,N$ and $D=R,A,B$. The etale-localization and standard-coordinate clauses of [lem-pur-dnc-coefficient-transport], for $R\to D$, say precisely
$$\lambda_D^H t_D^H=t_D^P T_D(\lambda_R^H).$$
Here $t_D^H$ denotes its restriction to $S'$ when necessary. The pullback/tensor comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] (for $R\to D$) and of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] (for $A\to B$) identify that restriction with the localized scalar extension. Step 3 also applies to $P$, and restriction of its equations for $H$ gives $t_B^H=q_HQ(t_A^H)$. Thus
$$\begin{aligned}
\lambda_B^Hq_HQ(t_A^H)&=\lambda_B^Ht_B^H
=t_B^PT_B(\lambda_R^H)\\
&=q_PQ(t_A^P)T_B(\lambda_R^H)
=q_PQ(\lambda_A^H)Q(t_A^H).
\end{aligned}$$
Cancel $Q(t_A^H)$ to obtain $\lambda_B^Hq_H=q_PQ(\lambda_A^H)$ for both $H=G,N$. The coefficient-composition identity for $P$ is [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities](2), and rebracketing and functoriality are [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](4). This is exactly the claimed identification of both comparisons with $q_{p_d,0}$; it proves commutativity with the actual localization identifications. The argument uses only invertible comparisons and functorial identities, so includes $d=0$, $m=n$ and empty schemes.
